analysis:
The only changed file is a test file, provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Service/ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift. The change is in replacementReplaysCurrentDesiredStateWithoutRevivingDeselectedAlias (head lines 537-567). The old test pushed a single desired-model entry (an alias successor) and expected it to be prefetched after resumeAfterModelSwitch. The new test pushes two entries: an alias successor outside the switched selection ("retained-alias", whose desiredBuild is a random org/current-UUID) and a desired build the selection holds (new-model). It asserts three things after resume: desiredPrefetchTargets == ["new-model"], no prefetch status is sent for the obsolete or successor builds, and desiredSwapDrop is empty.

The asserted behavior is that the production code filters deferred desired-model entries against the operator-selected model set. That keeps a coordinator-pushed desired_models frame from reviving a deselected alias or prefetching an unselected build. This is consistent with the existing boundary in TB-002/TB-003 and the retained model-switch controls, so it does not weaken them. This test change tightens the test's coverage.

The diff changes no production code, keys, attestation, encryption, cache handling, or authorization paths. The remaining lines are unchanged, including the rollback and hash-preservation tests and the autopilot ownership test. The test code adds no new attack surface: it uses temp directories and a mock coordinator. The patch excerpt is truncated, but the head text is fully visible for the changed region.

One integration question remains. The production filtering logic is not in this batch, so I could not verify that it matches what the test asserts. The next pass should confirm in ProviderLoop's desired-models handling and the deferred replay on resumeAfterModelSwitch that entries outside the active selection are dropped and that desiredSwapDrop is not populated for them. No finding is raised from the supplied evidence.
